label: False
claim: Due to Imran Khan's criticism of Macron's comments on Islam, French authorities cancelled the visas of 183 Pakistani citizens and deported 118 from the country.
doc: Macron described Islam as a religion "in crisis" worldwide and vowed to present a bill in December to strengthen France's church-state separation law. Pakistan's Prime Minister Imran Khan criticised Macron, accusing him of encouraging Islamophobia by attacking Islam rather than terrorists and deliberately provoking Muslims by encouraging the display of blasphemous cartoons. The tweets attributed to the Pakistani Consulate in France originated from @PakConsulateFr, which is not the official Twitter account of the Pakistani Consulate in France. No evidence was found that France cancelled Pakistani citizens' visas or deported any Pakistanis in connection with Khan's comments.
speaker: Consulate General Of Pakistan France

doc: Don Gaetz is the retired co-founder of VITAS Healthcare Corp., a hospice care provider, and also served as president of the National Hospice Organization. In 2004, VITAS was acquired by Chemed, the parent company of Roto-Rooter, for $400 million. A lawsuit against Chemed was filed in 2013—nine years after Don Gaetz sold the company—alleging fraud dating back to at least 2002. Don Gaetz was not a party to the lawsuit and denied that the matters in the complaint related to his work with Vitas. No evidence was found that Matt Gaetz personally worked for Chemed Corporation, Vitas Hospice Services, or Vitas Healthcare.

label: True

doc: As of October 31, 2020, the United States had recorded 230,512 COVID-19 deaths. Research indicates that the delayed U.S. pandemic response was devastating: 117,858 Americans died in the four months following the first 15 confirmed cases, compared to only 8,863 in Germany over an equivalent period. Scaling Germany's population to the size of the U.S., approximately 70% of U.S. coronavirus deaths—around 161,358 of the 230,512 total—might have been prevented had the U.S. acted as effectively as Germany.

label: False
claim: White House coronavirus adviser Dr. Anthony Fauci wrote a 2008 paper that found most 1918-1919 Spanish Influenza pandemic deaths were because of bacterial pneumonia from wearing masks.
doc: The majority of deaths in the 1918–1919 influenza pandemic likely resulted directly from secondary bacterial pneumonia caused by common upper respiratory tract bacteria, not from the influenza virus acting alone. The study in question does not mention masks and made no reference to deaths caused by wearing masks.
speaker: Dawn Hellewell

label: False
claim: Dr Anthony Fauci wrote a paper regarding the Spanish Flu and stated that the majority of deaths in 1918-1919 was because of bacterial pneumonia from wearing masks.
doc: Research published in The Journal of Infectious Diseases found that most victims of the 1918–1919 influenza pandemic succumbed to bacterial pneumonia following influenza virus infection, rather than to the virus acting alone. The pneumonia occurred when bacteria that normally inhabit the nose and throat invaded the lungs along a pathway created when the virus destroyed cells lining the bronchial tubes and lungs. NIAID Director Anthony Fauci stated: "The virus landed the first blow while bacteria delivered the knockout punch." Pathologist Jeffery Taubenberger examined lung tissue from 58 soldiers who died in 1918 and 1919, finding evidence ranging from primary viral pneumonia to severe secondary bacterial pneumonia. Medical experts agree that bacteria, not influenza viruses, were the greatest cause of death during the 1918 pandemic, and Dr Fauci's publication made no claim that masks caused flu deaths.

label: False
claim: India's imports from China increased by 27% during the period April-August 2020.
doc: India's imports from China declined sharply in 2020. From January to February 2020, India's imports from China were as low as US$9.5 billion, reflecting a 12.4 per cent trade decline in the initial two months of COVID-19. Imports fell to a record low of USD 3.2 billion in both April and May 2020, coinciding with pandemic-induced lockdowns, before recovering to USD 4.8 billion in June and USD 5.6 billion in July—nearly back to the pre-lockdown level of USD 5.8 billion in March. For the first seven months of 2020, India's imports from China totalled USD 32.2 billion, still down 24.7% year-on-year. Commerce and Industry Minister Piyush Goyal confirmed that imports from China declined by 27.63% during April–August 2020.
speaker: Pankaj Pachauri

label: True

doc: Between March and August 2020, the U.S. recorded 1,336,561 deaths, of which 150,541 (67%) were attributed directly to COVID-19. During the same period, 225,530 were 'excess' deaths—deaths occurring beyond what would normally be expected. Of those 225,530 excess deaths, 150,541 (approximately two-thirds) were attributed to COVID-19, leaving roughly one-third of excess deaths attributable to other causes.

University of Florida professor Michael McDonald estimated total 2020 general election turnout at 150 million voters, meaning approximately 2.2% of the electorate had voted by early October. label: False
claim: Zimbabwe recorded its first coronavirus Infection before 20 February 2020.
doc: Zimbabwe's Ministry of Health and Child Care confirmed on 20 February 2020 that a reported suspected COVID-19 case had been ruled out as negative, and that Zimbabwe remained coronavirus free at that time.
speaker: Zimbabwe Social Media News

label: False
claim: Ruth Bader Ginsburg was nominated and confirmed 43 days before an election.
doc: President Clinton announced Ruth Bader Ginsburg as a Supreme Court nominee on June 15, 1993, and she was confirmed by the United States Senate on August 3, 1993. There was no U.S. election 43 days after her confirmation in August 1993.
speaker: Jon Cook

label: False
claim: John Cammo was the only one to predict that President Trump would be infected with Covid-19.
doc: Many people predicted that Donald Trump would contract COVID-19; John Cammo was not the only person to do so.
speaker: John Cammo

label: False
claim: The fastest Supreme Court justice ever confirmed in the U.S. was 47 days.
doc: John Paul Stevens holds the record for the fewest days between Supreme Court nomination and confirmation at 19 days, followed by Amy Coney Barrett at 27 days. The overall average from nomination to final Senate vote is 68.2 days (median 69.0 days). Among the nine current Justices, the average is 72.1 days (median 73.0 days), with Amy Coney Barrett waiting the fewest days (27) and Clarence Thomas the greatest number (99).
speaker: Joe Biden

label: False
claim: In 2019, 10 million fell ill from tuberculosis and 1.5 million died but nobody needs to wears a mask for tuberculosis
doc: The 2011 Curry International Tuberculosis Center manual on tuberculosis infection control states that individuals with suspected or known infectious TB should wear a surgical mask when not in an airborne infection isolation room or a local exhaust ventilation enclosure, in order to block aerosols produced by coughing, talking, and breathing. Staff are to monitor patients for compliance and replace masks when damp. The Curry International Tuberculosis Center creates and disseminates resources and performs research to control and eliminate tuberculosis in the United States and internationally.

label: True
claim: Donald Trump is in federal court trying to do away with the Affordable Care Act, 100 million people with preexisting conditions like your mom would not have to pay more for their insurance under now.”
doc: The Affordable Care Act (ACA) provides individuals and families access to affordable health insurance, preventing insurers from refusing coverage based on gender or pre-existing conditions, eliminating lifetime or annual limits, allowing young adults to stay on family plans until age 26, and offering Medicare prescription drug discounts. The Trump administration asked the Supreme Court to repeal the ACA in its entirety, stating "the entire ACA act must fall", consistent with Trump's 2016 campaign pledge and Republican lawmakers' longstanding opposition to the law since its 2010 inception.
speaker: Joe Biden

label: True
claim: Carlos Gimenez approved a 67% pay raise for himself and increased his own pension.
doc: Senator Gimenez was earning around $150,000 after voluntarily cutting his salary when he became mayor in 2011. He subsequently increased his salary by 67% because he had been taking a pay cut since 2011. He also increased his own pension.
speaker: Debbie Mucarsel-Powell

label: False
claim: Kim Martin Morrow the CEO of Netflix has just been charged with 15 charges for child pornography and 31,000 files have been found on his personal computers for child porn from ages 8 and as young as toddlers.
doc: Reed Hastings is the founder and was the CEO of Netflix. As of 2021, Netflix has two Co-Chief Executive Officers: Reed Hastings and Ted Sarandos.
speaker: Marie Mares

label: False
claim: Development Control Department of the Abuja Metropolitan Management Council (AMMC), an agency of the Federal Capital Territory Administration (FCTA)of Nigeria, in 2020 marked 37 Estates for demolition.
doc: No estates in Nigeria were marked for demolition in 2020 by the Abuja Metropolitan Management Council.

label: False
claim: A US voter can vote 4 times because he got 4 vote by mail forms.
doc: Each eligible U.S. citizen is allowed to cast only one vote during elections—a basic tenet of democracy. A voter who received multiple envelopes from the Center for Voter Information received "Vote At Home Ballot Request Forms," not actual ballots.
speaker: James Snapp

label: False
claim: A Rafale Aircraft crashed during training and two pilots are dead.
doc: Rafale aircraft were being inducted into service at the time of the claim. None of the inducted aircraft crashed.
speaker: Aditi Chattopadhyay

label: True
claim: US state of Georgia has “almost 100,000 more COVID-19 cases, almost twice as many deaths and almost 600 more nursing home deaths than North Carolina, US.
doc: The claim was made during a debate on October 14, 2020. On that date, Georgia's health department reported 7,470 total COVID-19 deaths and 334,601 COVID-19 cases, while North Carolina's health department reported 3,856 total COVID-19 deaths and 236,407 confirmed cases. CMS reported 1,328 nursing home COVID-19 deaths in North Carolina and 1,897 nursing home COVID-19 deaths in Georgia.
speaker: Roy Cooper

label: False
claim: Donald Trump tweeted that he was donating $500,000 each toward the expenses of the two Los Angeles County sheriff's deputies who were shot and critically injured on September 12, 2020.
doc: The tweet in question did not come from Donald Trump's official Twitter account, @realDonaldTrump. Trump's official account made no mention of the officers shot and critically injured.
speaker: @RealDonaldTrwp

label: True
claim: Iran has stockpiled 10 times as much enriched uranium as it had in 2016.
doc: Under the 2015 Joint Comprehensive Plan of Action (JCPOA), Iran was restricted to a total enriched uranium stockpile of no more than 300 kg of up to 3.67% enriched uranium hexafluoride for 15 years, equivalent to 202.8 kg. Iran continued enrichment after the deal but did not enrich above 3.67% in 2016. By January 2020, a senior Iranian official claimed the stockpile had reached 1,200 kg, more than doubling in three months, while a separate report indicated a stockpile of around 2,105 kg of enriched uranium. The IAEA found approximately 550 kg of uranium hexafluoride enriched to less than 4.5% as of late 2019; if further enriched, this quantity could yield more than 30 kg of weapons-grade uranium, enough for one fission bomb.
speaker: Joe Biden

label: True
claim: Edo State in Nigeria has a 19% unemployment rate.
doc: The claim was made on 13 September 2020. According to data released by the Nigeria Bureau of Statistics, the unemployment rate in Edo State dropped from 25.1% in the third quarter of 2018 to 19% in the second quarter of 2020.
speaker: Edo State governor, Godwin Obaseki

label: False
claim: Netflix CEO Reed Hastings was arrested by the FBI after being caught with 13,000 files of child pornography.
doc: There is no evidence, nor any news reporting, to support the claim that Netflix CEO Reed Hastings was arrested for possession of child pornography.
speaker: Toronto today

label: False
claim: the Indian Government set up 5 coaching centres for UPSC exams, 4 of which were in Muslim universities.
doc: The Indian Government set up five training centres between 2009 and 2010 to provide underprivileged communities—including Scheduled Tribes, Scheduled Castes, women, and minorities—with free residential coaching for civil services and other government exams. One of the five centres is Jamia Millia Islamia, which was granted minority institution status by the NCMEI and can reserve up to 50% of seats for Muslims; however, the institution serves all underprivileged communities, not Muslims only. The government provides additional free coaching opportunities beyond the five centres, and none of the five centres are Muslim-only institutions.

label: False
claim: US Congress voted 49-46 to add the repeal of Section 230 — legislation which shields online platforms from liability for user-generated content — into the country’s annual defense bill in December 2020
doc: Section 230 of the 1996 Communications Decency Act protects online service providers from lawsuits based on user-generated content. A 49–46 Senate vote took place to confirm Nathan A. Simington of Virginia as a member of the Federal Communications Commission for a term of five years from July 1, 2019. The 2021 bill related to this vote contains no mention of Section 230.

label: False
claim: Nita Ambani is to give Rs 200 crore for Kangana Ranaut’s new studio
doc: No results confirm that Nita Ambani is giving Kangana Ranaut Rs 200 crore for the construction of a new studio.
speaker: Bahubali Ashok Singh

label: False
claim: $400,000 ... is more money than I’ve ever made” in a year
doc: Joe Biden's gross incomes above $400,000 since 1998 include: $407,009 in 2013, $11,031,309 in 2017, and $4,580,437 in 2018.
speaker: Joe Biden

label: True
claim: In England only 69.4% of COVID-19 contacts are now reached and asked to self-isolate.
doc: Between 20 August and 26 August 2020, 31,388 people were identified as having come into close contact with someone who tested positive for COVID-19 in the UK. Of these, 69.4% were reached and asked to self-isolate.
speaker: Jonathan Ashworth

label: False
claim: 80 million ballots for the US November 3 2020 election will be mailed to US voters who didn’t request them.
doc: Approximately 80 million mail ballots were expected to be cast in the 2020 U.S. election. This figure represents the estimated total number of all mail ballots, not unsolicited ones.
speaker: US President Donald Trump

label: False
claim: 53 Johannes Ramokhoase street Pretoria is a human trafficking hotspot.
doc: South African police stated that social media posts depicting a building on Johannes Ramokhoase Street in Pretoria's CBD as a human trafficking centre are fake news. Police confirmed the building is in fact a residential facility accommodating police officers.
speaker: 8teen

label: True
claim: Willie Obiano, the Governor of Anambra State in Nigeria, procured over 100 SUVs as gifts for Anambra state traditional monarchs.
doc: A photo exists of an SUV handover ceremony that took place at Dr Alex Ekwueme Square in Awka. All beneficiaries attended the ceremony, including the Chairman of the Anambra State Traditional Rulers Council, Igwe Nnaemeka Achebe, who also serves as Chairman of the South East Traditional Rulers Council.
speaker: @henryshield

label: False
claim: Donald Trump tweeted “THE NEXT 30 TO 60 DAYS WILL BE THE BIGGEST DRAINING OF THE SWAMP EVER”
doc: Donald Trump did not tweet "THE NEXT 30 TO 60 DAYS WILL BE THE BIGGEST DRAINING OF THE SWAMP EVER." The tweet was posted from a fake account impersonating Trump's real Twitter handle, originating from New Zealand.
speaker: Silver Bullion

label: False
claim: Between 2010 and 2018, the Uighur population had the region’s highest birthrate, at about 12 newborns per 1,000 people in Xinjiang, China.
doc: The Uyghur population is concentrated in the Xinjiang Uyghur Autonomous Region of northwest China, with approximately 10 million Uyghurs in China and at least 300,000 in Central Asian republics. The birthrate for Uyghurs in Xinjiang dropped from 14.85 per 1,000 in 2010 to 10.69 per 1,000 in 2018. In the predominantly Uyghur prefectures of Kashgar and Hotan, yearly birthrates between 2010 and 2018 ranged from 24.27 to 8.17 per 1,000, with an overall average of approximately 16+ and a 2018 figure of 8.17. Birth rates in Hotan and Kashgar plunged more than 60% from 2015 to 2018, compared to a 24% drop across Xinjiang and just 4.2% nationwide. The Uyghur birth rate of about 12 per 1,000 does not match official data from Xinjiang Statistical Yearbooks, and the 2018 figure for Hotan and Kashgar was below both regional and national averages. Researchers attribute the dramatic decline to a birth control campaign involving sterilisations, IUDs, and mandatory birth control measures.
speaker: Spokesperson for Chinese Ministry of Foreign affairs

label: False
claim: US President Donald Trump plans to cut social security, resulting in social security becoming permanently depleted by the middle of calendar year 2023.
doc: President Trump issued a memorandum ordering Treasury Secretary Steven Mnuchin to suspend Social Security payroll taxes for some employers and employees from September 1, 2020 until December 31, 2020. While the tax cut could potentially be made permanent, the White House stated it would have zero impact on Social Security, as an automatic contribution from the general fund would cover Social Security funding.
speaker: Joe Biden

label: False
claim: 450,000 people attended the Sturgis Motorcycle Rally in South Dakota, and there were only 88 positive Covid-19 tests, so a .02% infection rate.
doc: About 460,000 people attended the Sturgis Motorcycle Rally. South Dakota confirmed 124 COVID-19 cases tied to the rally as of September 8, and at least 290 people in 12 other states tested positive after attending. Based on 414 total cases out of 460,000 attendees, the infection rate was 0.09%, not 0.02%.
speaker: Bikers for Trump

label: False
claim: Sturgis Motorcycle Rally resulted in no more positive Covid results than the rest of the state, South Dakota, average stating 88 positive tests to Sturgis Rally, 0.02% infection rate of attendees.
doc: South Dakota reported 124 COVID-19 cases among state residents who attended the Sturgis Rally. Combined with cases from other states, a total of 414 cases were linked to the rally out of approximately 460,000 attendees, yielding an infection rate of 0.09%.
speaker: Bikers for Trump

label: False
claim: A 21 year old can have sex with an 11-year-old, and not be listed on the sex registry as a sex offender
doc: The legal age of consent in California is 18 years old, the age at which a person can legally marry and engage in sexual acts. For consensual sexual relations between a teenager aged 15 or older and a partner within 10 years of age, California law already granted judges discretion over sex offender registration for vaginal intercourse but mandated registration for oral and anal intercourse. Senator Scott Wiener introduced SB 145, which extends that same judicial discretion to other forms of intercourse, ending what the bill's proponents describe as discrimination against LGBT young people. SB 145 does not change whether particular behaviour is a crime or alter potential sentencing.

label: False
claim: Economic damage caused by the pandemic shows United States GDP (gross domestic product) falling by 33 percent compared to India's 23.9 percent drop.
doc: The United States and India report GDP growth and contraction differently. The U.S. GDP dropped by 9.1% during April to June 2020 on an annualised basis, while India's GDP contracted by 23.9%. When compared using the same reporting methodology, the U.S. GDP contraction during April to June 2020 was 9.1%.
speaker: S Gurumurthy

label: False
claim: In Belfast, the digital sector employs 26 per cent of the workforce.
doc: A Tech Nation "Jobs & Skills Report 2020" analysed job vacancy advertising in the UK from June to August 2020 using Adzuna data, and a Times article based on it stated that in Belfast and Cambridge the tech sector employs 26% of the workforce. However, using BRES data, the two relevant industrial sectors—information and communication, and professional, scientific, and technical—employed an estimated 32,927 people in Belfast, representing 14% of the city's workforce. Counting only IT and engineering roles of the type advertised on Adzuna, an estimated 18,041 people are employed in such jobs in Belfast, representing 7.8% of Belfast's jobs.
speaker: The Times

label: True
claim: In 2018, South African police service officers were accused of 217 cases of torture and 3,661 cases of assault.
doc: In the 2018/2019 year, 270 cases of torture and 3,835 cases of assault were brought against the South African police department.

label: False
claim: Since 2002, South Africa’s police force has grown by 50%.
doc: The South African police force employed 132,310 people in 2002/03 and 192,277 in 2018/19, representing a growth of 45.3% over that period.

label: True
claim: 558 people were killed by the police in 2018, while 201 people died in police custody
doc: Police violence has increased in South Africa. In 2018, South African police killed 558 people, and 201 additional people died in custody at the hands of South African police.

label: False
claim: The number of North American bison has been reduced to only twenty-seven individuals due to colonizers.
doc: The North American bison was nearly brought to extinction, though it was not reduced to only 27 individuals by colonisers. Through ongoing conservation work, bison have recovered from a low of fewer than 1,000 individuals; today, 19 herds in 12 states roam the American Plains, and about 500,000 bison live on preserves and ranches where they are raised for their meat.

label: True
claim: A crowdfunding campaign on the Christian site GiveSendGo solicited donations to help Kyle Rittenhouse, a 17-year-old accused of killing two people at a protest in Kenosha, Wisconsin.
doc: GiveSendGo, a Christian crowdfunding website, set up a fundraising account for Kyle Rittenhouse's legal defence. The site initially raised over $80,000 and subsequently reported raising more than $100,000 for Rittenhouse's defence.
speaker: Cassandra of Troy

label: False
claim: Donald trump said "We have already built 300 miles of border wall."
doc: When Trump began campaigning for president, the southwest border had 654 miles of primary barriers. Under Trump, that increased by three miles to 657 miles. The Trump administration mainly replaced barriers installed by previous administrations with new ones expected to be more effective. Mexico did not pay for any construction; American taxpayers covered the costs.
speaker: Donald Trump

label: False
claim: Donald Trump said: Biden "has pledged a $4 trillion tax hike on almost all American families."
doc: Joe Biden stated he would raise taxes for anyone making over $400,000 and impose no new taxes on anyone making under $400,000. Biden would also raise taxes on corporations by increasing the corporate income tax rate and imposing a corporate minimum book tax.
speaker: Donald Trump

label: False
claim: The Edo State government of Nigeria receives 600 million naira monthly as a security vote.
doc: Security votes are monthly budgetary allocations provided by Nigeria's federal government to the 36 states for financing security, disbursed at officials' discretion and not subject to legislative oversight or independent audit. Transparency International estimates these secretive cash expenditures add up to over $670 million (N241.2 billion) annually. In 2020, the Edo State government received 6.5 billion naira through security voting, equating to approximately 417 million naira per month.
speaker: Pastor Ize-Lyamu

label: True
claim: Kenosha police allowed Kyle Rittenhouse to walk away after he killed two protesters and injured a third with an AR-15-style rifle.
doc: According to eyewitness videos and the criminal complaint, Kyle Rittenhouse shot and killed Joseph Rosenbaum in a parking lot after Rosenbaum chased him and tried to grab his gun. Rittenhouse then began running down the street, tripped and fell, and was approached by Anthony Huber carrying a skateboard; Rittenhouse fired one round that killed Huber. He then fired a shot that hit Gaige Grosskreutz in the arm. Rittenhouse subsequently approached police at the scene. Kenosha Police Chief Daniel Miskinis defended his officers' actions, stating they did not see Rittenhouse as a threat and could not hear crowd yelling over other noise, as they were focused on injuries further down the street.
speaker: Gwen Moore

label: False
claim: The first night of the US Republican National Convention had 128.4 million viewers
doc: The first night of the 2020 Republican National Convention on Monday, August 24 was broadcast on cable and television networks. According to Nielsen, which statistically estimates the number of Americans watching TV, an estimated 17 million people tuned in to watch the first night of the convention.
speaker: Absolute Patriot states

label: Conflicting
claim: America went from 75,000 flu deaths last year in 2019 to almost 0 in 2020
doc: The U.S. Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC) estimated 21,909 flu deaths during the 2019-2020 flu season, a claim made via tweet during week 44 of the year, from October 26 to November 1. Flu season, as determined by elevated flu activity, varies from season to season, with activity typically beginning to increase in October, most often peaking between December and February, and remaining elevated into May. However, the CDC graph for flu deaths shows the line at 0 and going down for 2020 through to 2021, indicating that the U.S. recorded no flu deaths throughout the whole year of 2020.

label: Conflicting
claim: Donald Trump said that $15 an hour is too much for essential workers
doc: Donald Trump indicated he would consider a $15 per hour federal minimum wage, though he expressed a preference for leaving minimum wage decisions to individual states rather than implementing a federal mandate.
speaker: Joe Biden

label: Conflicting
claim: UK Employees unable to work in tier 3 areas will get a combination of Job Support Scheme and Universal Credit, which will mean they get 80% of their wages.
doc:
The UK introduced two major employment support schemes during the coronavirus crisis. The initial Furlough Scheme applied across the UK and covered up to 80% of an employee's salary for the hours they couldn't work, up to a maximum of £2,500 per month. This was subsequently replaced by the expanded Job Support Scheme, under which staff at UK companies told to close would receive 67% of their wages from the government. The Job Support Scheme ran for six months through to 30th April 2021.

Under the Job Support Scheme, employees must work at least 33% of their usual hours for the job to be considered 'viable' and therefore eligible. The scheme operates through a tripartite contribution model: the Government pays a third of the hours not worked (up to a cap), the employer contributes a third, and the remaining unpaid third represents the employee's contribution. This structure means an employee earns 77% of their normal wage where the Government contribution has not been capped.

For example, an employee working 5 days a week and earning £350 weekly, if placed on the scheme working only 2 days a week (40% of usual hours), would receive £140 from their employer for days worked and £140 in support for the 3 days not worked (two-thirds of the £210 value), totaling £280 or 80% of their normal wage. The Government would provide a grant of £70 (one-third of hours not worked, equivalent to 20% of normal wages) to the employer. However, this scheme is considerably less generous than the previous Furlough Scheme, and it remains unclear whether it will provide tangible benefit to company directors typically paid a modest PAYE salary at the National Insurance earnings threshold.
speaker: Boris Johnson

label: Conflicting
claim: NBC News Kristen Welker gave thousands of dollars to Obama, Clinton and Biden, is registered as a Democrat & her family spent Christmas with the Obamas at the White House.
doc: A viral Facebook post made false claims about NBC News debate moderator Kristen Welker, alleging that she gave thousands of dollars to Obama, Clinton, and Biden, is registered as a Democrat, and spent Christmas with the Obamas at the White House. However, there is no record of Welker donating thousands of dollars to Democrats. Her White House visit during Christmas was for the annual White House press Christmas party hosted by Obama at the time, an event that other journalists also attended.
speaker: Ray Martorella

label: Conflicting
claim: More people who wear masks become sick with COVID-19 compared to non-mask wearers
doc: A study involving 314 participants examined the relationship between mask usage and COVID-19 infection. Of these participants, 154 had tested positive for COVID-19 as case-patients, while 160 had tested negative as control participants. When surveyed about mask usage, 11 people reported never wearing a mask, while 216 people reported always wearing a mask.
speaker: Jordan Davidson

label: Conflicting
claim: New Zealand spends less on pensions than most wealthy countries, spending 4.4 per cent of GDP
doc: New Zealand currently spends 4.8% of GDP on pensions, which is less than most wealthy countries.
speaker: Winston Peters

label: Conflicting
claim: Govt of India is providing money to bereaved families of COVID-19 - Insurance benefits for Covid-19 deaths can be claimed under the schemes of PMJJBY and PMSBY.
doc: The PMJJBY insurance scheme is available to people in the age group of 18 to 50 years who possess a bank account and provide their consent to join or enable auto-debit. The PMSBY scheme, on the other hand, is available to people in the age group of 18 to 70 years with a bank account who give their consent to join or enable auto-debit on or before 31st May for the coverage period from 1st June to 31st May on an annual renewal basis. Under the PMSBY scheme, the risk coverage provides Rs. 2 lakh for accidental death and full disability, and Rs. 1 lakh for partial disability. Regarding government provisions for bereaved families of COVID-19 victims, while the PMJJBY scheme is applicable to COVID-19 deaths, there are certain conditions with respect to the eligibility and claim process that must be met.
speaker: Funds4-covid19.com

label: Conflicting
claim: US Miami-Dade County Mayor Carlos Giminez kept his taxpayer-funded Mercedes-Benz after slashing $400 million in government jobs and spending.
doc: J.C. Planas, an attorney for the Gimenez campaign and a former state legislator, stated that when Gimenez was a county commissioner, he was entitled to the same car allowances as all the commissioners. During his time as commissioner, Gimenez drove a Mercedes-Benz ML and prior to that a Mercedes-Benz E320. Car allowances, or the use of city-owned cars, constitute one piece of an official's compensation package. As a county commission official, Gimenez approved a cut of $400 to the car allowance. However, Gimenez does not currently have a car allowance.
speaker: Debbie Mucarsel-Powell

label: Conflicting
claim: Kyle Rittenhouse failed to appear at his court hearing in Lake County, Illinois, on 28th August 2020 and was given an extra month to comply.
doc: Kyle Rittenhouse did not appear for his first hearing on 28 August 2020, as his initial hearing was delayed by the judge.
speaker: Emilie Marie Blake

label: Conflicting
claim: Donald Trump said "When the anarchists started ripping down our statues and monuments, right outside, I signed an order immediately, 10 years in prison."
doc: Trump signed an executive order that authorizes a penalty of up to 10 years in prison for damaging federal property, though it does not mandate an automatic 10-year prison sentence. This was not a new law.
speaker: Donald Trump
